Rashi on Gittin 44a:10:1.english: Examine your mekhilta - In the Mishnah [teaching] arranged for you, to know what we should reply:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:10:2.hebrew: המוכר ביתו לעובד כוכבים - בארץ ישראל, דאמר קרא: "לא תחנם" — לא תתן להם חנייה בקרקע (ע"ז דף כ.):
Rashi on Gittin 44a:10:2.english: One who sells his house to an idolater - In the Land of Israel, as the verse says: "You shall not show them favor [lo techanem]" — [meaning] you shall not grant them a resting place [chaniyah] in the land (Avodah Zarah 20a):

Rashi on Gittin 44a:10:3.english: And he writes - a document for him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:10:4.hebrew: ומעלהו בערכאות שלהן - לחותמו, אף על פי שחשיבות הוא להם:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:10:4.english: And he registers it in their courts - to have it signed, even though it is [an expression of] importance to them:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:11:1.hebrew: ודילמא - הא דלא גזור רבנן בהך, דילמא אתי לזבוני מדעתו:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:11:1.english: And perhaps - that which the Rabbis did not decree regarding this [case], lest he come to sell [it] willingly:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:11:2.hebrew: הני מילי בית - דלא סגי ליה לאינש בלא בית, ולא עבידי אינשי דמזבני:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:11:2.english: This matter [applies only to] a house - since a person cannot do without a house, and people do not ordinarily sell [them].

Rashi on Gittin 44a:11:3.hebrew: אתי לזבוני - וגזרינן בהא אטו מכירה דעלמא, ולא תפשוט:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:11:3.english: He will come to sell him - And we enact a decree in this [case] on account of an ordinary sale, and [thus] you cannot resolve [the dilemma]:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:12:1.english: Rabbi Ami sent to them - to those who asked him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:12:2.english: From me, Ami bar Natan, Torah shall go forth - [meaning,] this ruling [goes forth] to Israel:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:13:1.english: He is penalized - to redeem [him] from the hand of the idolater:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:14:1.hebrew: דוקא או לאו דוקא - דלא קנסינן ליה כולי האי, וגוזמא קאמר:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:14:1.english: Specifically, or not specifically - [Not specifically, meaning] that we do not penalize him so much, and he is speaking in exaggeration:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:14:2.hebrew: עד עשרה - אלמא בהנך דקנוס רבנן במכירה דידהו, לא קנוס כולי האי:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:14:2.english: Up to ten [times its value] - Thus, in those [cases] where the Rabbis imposed a penalty for selling them, they did not penalize [the seller] so much.

Rashi on Gittin 44a:14:3.hebrew: אין מוכרין בהמה גסה - גזירה משום שאלה ושכירות ונסיוני, במסכת ע"ז (דף טו.):
Rashi on Gittin 44a:14:3.english: One may not sell a large animal [to a gentile] - [This is] a decree on account of lending, renting, and testing [it], [as taught] in Tractate Avodah Zarah (15a):

Rashi on Gittin 44a:15:1.hebrew: שאני עבד - כלומר, לעולם אימא לך דעבד דוקא, ושאני עבד כו':
Rashi on Gittin 44a:15:1.english: A slave is different - That is to say, in fact, I can tell you that [it applies] specifically to a slave, and a slave is different, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:16:1.hebrew: או לאו דוקא - דאי בעו מיניה טפי, קנסינן ליה עד דפריק, ואורחא דמלתא הוא דנקט:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:16:1.english: Or not specifically - for if they [the gentiles] demand more from him, we penalize him until he redeems [the slave], and it is [merely] the usual way of speaking that he used:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:16:2.hebrew: עד מאה - וקס"ד ה"ה לעבד:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:16:2.english: Up to one hundred - And [the Gemara] initially assumes [that] the same applies to a slave:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:17:1.hebrew: שאני עבד דלא הדר ליה - כלומר, דילמא תרוייהו דוקא; ועבד היינו טעמא דלא קנסוהו כולי האי, דלא הדר למריה בתר דפריק ליה, דהא תנן: "יצא לחירות":
Rashi on Gittin 44a:17:1.english: A slave is different, as he does not return to him - That is to say, perhaps both [rulings] are exact, and [with regard to] a slave, this is the reason they did not penalize him so much: because he does not return to his master after he redeems him, for we have learned [in the Mishnah]: "He goes out to freedom":

Rashi on Gittin 44a:18:1.hebrew: ופרכינן אלא בהמה מ"ט קנסינן ליה כולי האי משום דהדרה ליה ליקנסיה טפי חד - מכדי דמיה היה לך לקונסו יותר מן העבד ותו לא, הואיל וטעמא משום דהדרה ליה הוא — אין כאן אלא כדי דמיה, ואתה קונסו מי' עד ק'? אוי לו בחזרה זו:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:18:1.english: And we ask: Rather, [regarding] an animal, what is the reason we penalize him so much — because it returns to him? Let us penalize him one more - [By] the amount of its value you should penalize him more than [for] a slave, and no more. Since the reason is that it returns to him, there is here only [a gain of] its value, yet you penalize him from ten [times its value] up to a hundred [times]? Woe to him for this return:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:18:2.english: It is an uncommon matter - that they would sell him [a slave] to an idolater:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:19:1.english: What is [the law] as to whether they penalize his son - [requiring him] to redeem him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:19:2.hebrew: אם תימצי לומר - הך דמבעיא לן בבכורות: כהן הצורם אוזן הבכור, ועבר משום "כל מום לא יהיה בו", דאמרי' התם: לא ישחט עולמית, ומבעיא לן: צרם ומת, מהו שיקנסו בנו אחריו? ואם תימצי לומר בההיא דקנסוהו — הא דהכא לא מיפשט לן מינה, דהתם קא עבד אבוה איסורא דאורייתא, אבל מוכר עבדו לעובד כוכבים — איסורא דרבנן הוא דעבד:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:19:2.english: If you say - [This refers to] that [dilemma] which was raised for us in [Tractate] Bekhorot: [regarding] a Kohen who slits the ear of a firstborn [animal], thereby transgressing [the prohibition] "there shall be no blemish in it" — for we say there [that] it may never be slaughtered — and it was raised as a dilemma for us: [if] he slit [it] and died, what is [the law as to] whether they penalize his son after him? And [even] if you say in that case that they penalized him, this [case] here cannot be resolved for us from it; for there, his father committed a Torah prohibition, whereas one who sells his slave to a gentile — it is a rabbinic prohibition that he committed:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:1:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן ואיבעית אימא בשלוה על מנת למשכנו ולא משכנו - הא דשדה, כגון שלוה העובד כוכבים מישראל על מנת שאם לא אפרע לזמן פלוני, בא ומשכנני מקרקע זו ותהא שלך; והא דקתני "פטורה מן המעשר", כל זמן שלא בא ישראל ומשכנו — דאע"ג דמטא זמניה הויא בחזקת העובד כוכבים, ואם היה ישראל נוטל חלק בפירות פטורה מן המעשר; וגבי עבד כי האי גוונא קנסוה רבנן לישראל, ואע"פ שלא משכנו העובד כוכבים עדיין בעבד זה, קנסוהו הואיל ועבר זמנו ולא פרע:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:1:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "And if you wish, say: [It is] where he borrowed on condition to take it as collateral, and he did not take it as collateral" - That [case] of the field [is], for example, where the idolater borrowed from a Jew on condition that "if I do not pay by such-and-such a time, come and take this land from me as collateral and it shall be yours"; and that which it teaches, "[it is] exempt from the tithe" as long as the Jew has not come and taken it as collateral — [this is because] even though its time has arrived, it is [still] in the possession of the idolater, and [even] if the Jew was taking a share of the produce, it is exempt from the tithe; and regarding a slave in such a case, the Rabbis penalized the Jew: even though the idolater has not yet taken this slave as collateral, they penalized him since his time passed and he did not pay:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:1.english: He collected him - [i.e.,] the idolater [collected] the slave:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:2.hebrew: בחובו - שהיה לו על ישראל, והוא לא מכרו לו ולא לוה עליו:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:2.english: For his debt - [A debt] that he [the gentile] had against a Jew, and he [the Jew] neither sold [the slave] to him nor borrowed against him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:3.hebrew: סיקריקון - בשעה שישראל מופקרין להריגה, ואמר לעובד כוכבים: "שא קרקע זו או עבד זה והניחני":
Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:3.english: A Sicarius - At a time when Jews are abandoned to slaughter, and [a Jew] says to a gentile: "Take this land or this slave and leave me [alive]":

Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:4.hebrew: לא יצא לחירות - דאונס הוא, וליכא למקנסיה:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:2:4.english: He is not emancipated - Because it is [a case of] duress, and there is no [reason] to penalize him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:3:1.english: He is obligated to tithe - for it, as he is like a seller:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:3:2.english: In anparot [unjust seizure] - [This means a sheer] loss:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:4:1.hebrew: דקא משתרשי ליה - הרי נהנה מהם שפורע חובו, הילכך לענין עישור חייב במעשר. ומיהו גבי עבד, קנסא משום מכירה היא, וזה לא מכר מדעתו, אלא שלא לרצונו גבאו, ואמאי נקנסיה:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:4:1.english: Because he profits [from them] - Behold, he benefits from them, as he repays his debt [with them]; therefore, regarding tithing, he is obligated [to separate] tithe. However, regarding a slave, the penalty is on account of a sale, and this [owner] did not sell [him] of his own accord; rather, [the creditor] collected him against his will — so why should we penalize him?

Rashi on Gittin 44a:5:1.hebrew: פרהנג - מציק ושם עלילות, ומכרו לו בדמי אנפרותו שהעליל עליו:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:5:1.english: Parhang - An oppressor who brings false charges, and [the owner] sold [the slave] to him for the sum of his extortionate claim that he brought against him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:6:1.english: He should have appeased [him] - with something else:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:6:2.english: And he did not appease [him] - and [instead] he handed him over to him willingly:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:7:1.english: For thirty days - After thirty [days] he will return to him:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:7:2.hebrew: לפרהנג עובד כוכבים - וקס"ד שמכרו לעבוד עבודת המלך עד זמן פלוני ולשוב:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:7:2.english: To a gentile [government] official - And it was initially assumed [that he sold him] to perform the king's service until a certain time and [then] to return [to his master]:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:8:1.hebrew: חוץ ממלאכתו - "גופו קנוי לך, ובלבד שלא תשתעבד בו", שלא מכרו אלא להשיאו לשפחתו לולדות, דהשתא לא מפקע ממצות לחלל שבתות. א"נ, מכרו למלאכתו חוץ משבתות וימים טובים, מהו:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:8:1.english: Aside from his labor - [Meaning, the master said to the gentile:] "His person is acquired by you, provided that you do not subjugate him [for labor]," for he only sold him to marry him to his [the gentile's] maidservant for offspring, so that now he is not removed from mitzvot [so as] to desecrate Shabbatot. Alternatively, [if] he sold him for his labor aside from Shabbatot and Festivals, what is [the law]?

Rashi on Gittin 44a:8:2.hebrew: לגר תושב - שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים, ואוכל נבילות:
Rashi on Gittin 44a:8:2.english: To a ger toshav [resident alien] - [one] who accepted upon himself not to practice idolatry, and eats unslaughtered meat [neveilot]:

Rashi on Gittin 44a:8:3.english: Resolve at least [one] - [It is] a Baraita:

Tosafot on Gittin 44a:10:1.hebrew: וכותב ומעלה בערכאות שלהם - פירש בקונטרס: אף על פי דחשיבות הוא להן. וקשה, דשטרות העולין בערכאות של עובדי כוכבים מכשרינן, ולא מפלגינן בין לכתחילה בין לדיעבד. ומפרש רבינו תם, דאע"ג דנראה כמקיים המקח, שרי הכא. וההיא דפרק קמא דע"ז (דף יג.): "הולכין ליריד של עובדי כוכבים ולוקחים מהן בהמה ועבדים, מפני שהוא כמציל מידם, ומעלה בערכאות של עובדי כוכבים" — התם נמי מקיים המקח ומתפרסם הדבר שמהנה לעבודת כוכבי', ואפי' הכי שרי:
Tosafot on Gittin 44a:10:1.english: And he writes and registers [the sale] in their courts - Rashi explained: [This is permitted] even though it confers importance upon them. And this is difficult, for we validate documents that are registered in idolaters' courts, and we do not distinguish between [doing so] initially and after the fact! Rather, Rabbeinu Tam explains that even though he appears to be validating the sale, it is permitted here. And [as for] that [baraita] in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (13a): "One may go to an idolaters' fair and purchase animals and slaves from them, because it is like rescuing [them] from their hands, and one may register [the sale] in the idolaters' courts" — there too, he is validating the sale and it becomes publicized that he is benefiting idolatry, and even so it is permitted:

Tosafot on Gittin 44a:14:1.hebrew: או לאו דוקא - פירש בקונטרס דלא קנסינן ליה כולי האי, וגוזמא קאמר. וקשה, דאם כן איזה שיעור יהיב? דאכתי לא ידע ההיא דקונסין אותו עד עשרה, דנימא ביה ההוא שיעורא. ונראה לפרש: "או לאו דוקא" — אלא אפילו ביותר ממאה קנסינן ליה עד דפריק, כענין שפי' בקונטרס באיכא דאמרי. ומייתי מבהמה דקונסין אותו עד עשרה בדמיה — אלמא לאו דוקא, דהוא הדין טפי, כדקאמר הכא "עד מאה" גבי עבדים; והוא הדין דהכא לאו דוקא:
Tosafot on Gittin 44a:14:1.english: Or not specifically - Rashi explained that we do not penalize him so much, and [the Gemara] spoke with exaggeration. But this is difficult: if so, what limit does he give? For [the questioner] did not yet know that [statement of Reish Lakish] that they penalize him up to ten [times], that we should say [he meant] that limit! Rather, it seems [preferable] to explain: "or not specifically" — rather, even for more than a hundred [times] we penalize him until he redeems [him], similar to what Rashi explained in [the] "ikka de'amrei" [version]. And [the Gemara] brings [a proof] from [the case of] an animal, where they penalize him up to ten [times] its value — thus [we see that] it is not specific, for the same applies to more [than ten], as [the Gemara] says here "up to a hundred" regarding slaves; and the same applies here, [that "up to a hundred"] is not specific:

Tosafot on Gittin 44a:19:1.hebrew: התם דאיסורא דאורייתא - ובפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות לד:) גבי צרם אוזן הבכור קאמר דליכא למיפשט מהכא, דשאני עבד דמפקע ליה ממצות. אם כן, הוה מצי למימר הכא: אם תימצי לומר דהתם לא קנסו, הכא קנסו, משום דמפקע ליה ממצות; וכן התם הוה מצי למימר איפכא כי הכא:
Tosafot on Gittin 44a:19:1.english: There, it is a Torah prohibition - And in the chapter [entitled] Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 34b), regarding one who slit the ear of a firstborn, [the Gemara] says that one cannot resolve [that dilemma] from here, because a slave is different, as [selling him] removes him from [observing] mitzvot. If so, [the Gemara] could have said here: "If you say that there they did not penalize [the son], here they did penalize [him] because [selling him] removes him from mitzvot"; and likewise there it could have said the opposite, like here:

Tosafot on Gittin 44a:1:1.hebrew: בשלוה על מנת למשכנו כו' - פירש בקונטרס: שאם לא אפרע עד זמן פלוני, בא ומשכנני מקרקע זו ותהא שלך; וכל זמן שלא בא ישראל ומשכנו, הוי בחזקת עובד כוכבים. וגבי עבד כי האי גוונא, קנסוה רבנן לישראל הואיל ועבר הזמן ולא פרע, ואע"פ שלא משכנו עדיין. וקשה, דהוה ליה למימר "אידי ואידי דמטא זמניה"! לכך נראה, דאתא לשנויי שנויא קמא: "הא דמטא זמניה, והא דלא מטא זמניה"; והא דאקשינן "גבי עבד דמטא זמניה צריכא למימד" — בשלוה על מנת למשכנו ולא משכנו, דס"ד כיון דלא משכנו עדיין לא יצא לחירות, קא משמע לן דהואיל ובידו למשכנו, דיוצא לחירות:
Tosafot on Gittin 44a:1:1.english: Where he borrowed on the condition to take it as collateral, etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: [The borrower says,] "If I do not repay by such-and-such a time, come and take this land from me as collateral, and it shall be yours." And as long as the Jew has not come and taken it as collateral, it remains in the possession of the gentile [and is exempt from tithes]. And with regard to a slave in a similar case, the Rabbis penalized the Jew since the time passed and he did not repay, even though [the gentile] has not yet taken him as collateral. However, this is difficult, for [the Gemara] should have said, "Both this case and that case are where the time has arrived"! Therefore, it appears that [this statement] comes to resolve [the objection raised against] the first answer — "This [case] is where its time has arrived, and that [case] is where its time has not arrived" — and [as for] that which we asked, "With regard to a slave whose time has arrived, need it be said [that he is emancipated]?" — [the Gemara answers that it is needed] in a case where he borrowed on the condition to take him as collateral, and he did not [yet] take him as collateral; for it might have entered your mind [that] since he has not yet taken him as collateral, he does not go free. [Therefore, it] teaches us that since it is in his power to take him as collateral, he goes free:

Tosafot on Gittin 44a:5:1.hebrew: המוכר עבדו לפרהנג עובד כוכבים - פי' בקונטרס: מציק ושם עלילות, ומכרו לו באותן דמים שהעליל. וקשה, דלא שייך על זה לשון מכירה, ולישנא "שהיה לו לפייס ולא פייס" לא משמע הכי, ועוד דמדמי למוכרו לשלשים יום. ונראה דהפרהנג נוטל עבדו על כורחו, אלא שנותן לו דמים; לכך פריך דאמאי יצא לחירות, כיון דהוי בעל כורחו כמו גבאו בחובו. ומשני דהיה לו לפייס, דכיון דנותן דמים, ודאי היה מתפייס בדבר מועט. ומדמי לו נמי למוכרו לשלשים יום, דאחר שגומר מלאכתו דרכו להחזירו לישראל, וישראל מחזיר לו הדמים:
Tosafot on Gittin 44a:5:1.english: One who sells his slave to a gentile official [parhang] - Rashi explained [that a parhang is] an oppressor who brings false charges, and [the owner] sold [the slave] to him for that money which he falsely claimed. And this is difficult, for the term "selling" does not apply to this, and the wording "that he should have appeased [him] and did not appease [him]" does not imply this, and furthermore, [the Gemara] compares it to one who sells [his slave] for thirty days. Rather, it appears that the parhang takes his slave against his will, except that he gives him money [for him]; therefore [the Gemara] asks why he goes free, since it was against his will, like [the case where a creditor] collected him for his debt. And [the Gemara] answers that he should have appeased [him], for since [the parhang] gives money, he certainly would have been appeased with a small amount. And it also compares it to one who sells [his slave] for thirty days, because after he finishes his work, it is his practice to return him to the Jew, and the Jew returns the money to him:
